title: No single polynomial inequality defines a real binary Gram locus

abstract.source_tex: For a real tensor with \(n\) binary factors, consider the determinants of its one-mode Gram matrices as the tensor ranges over the closed Frobenius unit ball. For every \(n\geq3\), this locus cannot be defined by one polynomial nonnegativity condition in the determinant coordinates, even after imposing the cube bounds or the known convex-hull inequalities. This answers Seigal's single-polynomial question negatively for \(n\geq4\). The proof combines established qubit marginal polygon inequalities, an explicit real three-factor realization, a multiplicity obstruction, and exact zero-determinant slices. A strictly positive rational counterexample also refutes the proposed polynomial. Our theorem was recorded in a September 30, 2026 GitHub submission. Ferudun's October 2, 2026 preprint gives an overlapping stronger theorem; we credit it and record the chronology without claiming exclusive priority or certifying mutual independence.
